answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Binding. Each identity commits a cipher of its next-epoch action plan; when the epoch closes, the revealed plan must match the prior commitment within a tolerance window. A mismatch freezes the identity's outgoing transfers until it re-commits and completes a probation epoch. Sybils splitting into many fresh identities face a vine-like dependency: each new identity inherits the freeze history of any predecessor sharing a commitment lineage. Attackers must fund every clone through full probation, and a velvet constraint caps lineage depth,
